source_patient: Clinical Record 1 of a two-patient clinical report (the 64-year-old man). Clinical Record 2 (hepatic abscess) was not used.
disease_label_per_paper: Acute Q fever complicated by splenic abscess
presentation_summary: 64-year-old man living in metropolitan Cairns presented with 2 days of confusion; smoker, otherwise well; buried a dead bandicoot found in his garden 2 weeks before presentation (gloves, no face mask).
On admission febrile 38.7 C, hypotensive 88/50 mmHg, hypoxic respiratory failure with SpO2 92% on high-flow nasal prongs FiO2 0.45 at 40 L/min.
Platelets 51 x10^9/L, creatinine 246 umol/L (acute kidney injury), total bilirubin 36 umol/L, ALT 101 U/L, AST 337 U/L.
CT: bilateral bronchopneumonic changes, hepatomegaly, splenomegaly with a 3.9 cm lesion in the inferior pole.

confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: Repeat CT imaging revealed ongoing multilobar pneumonia and a splenic abscess

confirmatory_findings.finding: Initial working diagnosis severe community-acquired pneumonia; final paper diagnosis acute Q fever complicated by splenic abscess
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: He was diagnosed with severe community-acquired pneumonia ... We describe two patients in Far North Queensland with acute Q fever. One patient had their infection complicated by a splenic abscess

actual_treatment: intensive care unit admission for vasopressor support
doxycycline 100 mg twice daily, continued for 3 months

outcome.source_text_value: He continued doxycycline and, following clinical improvement and resolution of the splenic abscess on repeat imaging, he was able to cease after 3 months of therapy.

quality_warnings: Paper is a two-patient clinical report; only Clinical Record 1 is structured here.
Oxygen saturation 92% was measured on high-flow oxygen with FiO2 0.45, not on room air; FiO2 recorded as separate satellite axis.
Hepatomegaly and splenomegaly were CT findings, not bedside examination findings.
Vasopressor support is treatment and is kept out of ranking; the hemodynamic evidence is the admission blood pressure 88/50 mmHg.
Pathogen PCR/serology, repeat CT splenic abscess, aspirate PCR, treatment, and course are non-ranking confirmatory evidence.
No heart rate or respiratory rate reported at presentation.
